by: product-os-keeper, for #1021 (reorganise the business intents): BI-10 (Standards, structure, settings and memory) close
source: The product owner's reply of 2026-11-11, recorded in .garura/project/issues/1021/context/bi-10-close/approval.md: "Yes to domains opening paragraph as Yes to the six capability pages."

changes.old: This domain turns a business intent into working code that a check from the outside can prove. It serves the product owner, who names the work, the technical lead, who designs it, and the developer, who builds it. It specifies the product, sets the project's design, and builds the work test first. It writes the eval that says if the work is met before the work is built, and it never gives a builder the eval or the tests: a check flags each build session that read them. It then tests the built work from outside the builder, by its evals and against the levels, surfaces, designs and standards set before the build. Once the product is in use, it takes in how the product is used, what people say about it and what its competitors do, works out what consumers want, and turns that into new features or changes to the model, as recommendations to the product owner or on their own where the product owner allows it. It also gets Garura itself into a project, sets the project up for it, keeps it current, and serves whichever coding tool the team works in. It also lands every change the same way, with an outside review and a person's yes, and gives people one tool to review what agents made. It also orchestrates the work: it chooses and orders what runs next, runs plays as loops, tracks the work in the team's tracker, records each decision on how the project is built as an ADR, and gives every gate a way past. It does not release the work or run the product.

changes.old: It matters because agents build from what they are given. In this intent's words: "Agents follow the rules and memory they're given, so a loose rule or a wrong page reaches every later decision." And the standard is written for more than Garura's own repository: it is "written so that a team can take it and build its own harness the same way". It sits in software delivery planning with the other capabilities of Standards, structure, settings and memory. The domain's first paragraph does not name them yet; widening it is owed at this intent's close.

It sits in software delivery planning with the other capabilities of Standards, structure, settings and memory. The domain's first paragraph does not name them yet; widening it is owed at this intent's close.
